solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 28-across

clue.text: Diverting work from triumvirate on board

parts.note: a triumvirate is a ruling group of three men
on board a vessel is afloat in a boat

explanation.surface: A distraction devised by a ruling trio while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel of a Thames boating trip; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerome K. Jerome novel is a famously amusing book, an entertaining piece of writing.

clue.text: Pulls apart and climbs quickly?

definitions.meaning: to rip paper or cloth into pieces
to rush up a hill or stairs, the question mark flagging the playful second sense

explanation.definitionFit: Ripping something to shreds, and also racing upward at speed, are both senses of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Tombstone may have this in cathedral city

parts.note: gravestones often carry the letters RIP, rest in peace
in and on both mean happening or in progress, as a show that is on

explanation.surface: Graves in a cathedral city bearing a familiar inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP (requiescat in pace) is carved on headstones; Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon in North Yorkshire has a cathedral and so holds city status.

clue.text: Partner no longer battles for demands

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
military actions are battles

explanation.surface: A former spouse who no longer fights over what is being asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactions are payments or requirements forcibly required, that is, demands.

clue.text: Rugby chap, centre for Leicester

definitions.meaning: Harry ... is Tom Brown's friend at Rugby School in Tom Brown's Schooldays
Leicester sits in the ... Midlands, the eastern half of central England

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby here is the English public school, not the sport; Leicester is a city in the East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry East is a schoolboy character at Rugby, and the compass point names Leicester's part of the Midlands.

clue.text: Perverse pride in son coming first, being brilliant

indicators.note: the words in son are placed ahead of the rearranged word
perverse means contrary or wayward, so the following word is twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Contrary pride in a son who leads the way, showing brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perverse' gives PIRED from 'pride'; 'coming first' sends 'in' and S ahead of it, though the clue prints them after. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspired performance is one of outstanding, dazzling quality.

clue.text: Having succeeded with ace, established advantage

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
S is a genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
something set is fixed or established

explanation.surface: A tennis player who has won with an ace has secured the advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins S to A, which comes first; S for succeeded is used in family trees.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful resource or quality that gives a benefit.

clue.text: On the top of lager, possibly it's excessive

parts.note: over means on top of

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the following word could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A head on a pint of lager that is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LAGER into LARGE; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlarge is too big, beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Used coaches to get prepared for sport

definitions.meaning: coached or made fit for a game

explanation.definitionFit: Going by rail, and having been drilled for competition, are two senses of the same past tense.

clue.text: Article tells about judges

indicators.note: about means the word for tells goes around the article

parts.note: to apprise someone is to tell or inform them
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article reports on the judiciary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tells' looks like the verb of the surface's article, but it supplies the word for informing, which goes 'about' the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess or evaluate, as a judge weighs evidence.

clue.text: City given another name when burnt

definitions.text: City given another name when burnt

parts.words: City given another name when burnt
parts.note: add another N (name) to this Tuscan city and you get the brown pigment that is sold as burnt sienna

explanation.walkthrough: N is an abbreviation for name; burnt sienna is an artist's earth colour spelt with a double N.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a Tuscan city whose name, with an extra N, labels a brown pigment.

clue.text: Boy attending a musical performance

parts.note: a son is a boy
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: A lad going to a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is an instrumental piece, played as a recital work.

clue.text: Make shots and runs in this oddly, hit ball mainly to leg

definitions.text: Make shots and runs in this

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are jumbled
mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: on is the cricket term for the leg side

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction to strike the ball largely towards the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims one letter; 'oddly' rearranges the result with HIT into BIATHL. The cricket picture hides a winter event of skiing and rifle shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The biathlon combines cross-country skiing with rifle shooting, so competitors race and fire at targets.

clue.text: Concern for victim

definitions.meaning: a responsibility, as in 'that's not my business'
a dupe or easy mark for a swindler

explanation.definitionFit: The bird's name is idiom for one's own affair and slang for a gullible target.

clue.text: Officer you spotted, say, and deferentially salute

parts.note: GEN is short for general, an army officer

indicators.note: say signals the next words are to be taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: you flecked: 'you' sounds like U and flecked means spotted

explanation.surface: An officer who has caught sight of you, and a respectful greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the sound of 'you flecked'; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To genuflect is to bend the knee as a sign of reverence, a deep bow of respect.

clue.text: Relaxed in such classes, not … needing to work

definitions.text: in such classes, not … needing to work
definitions.meaning: describes the idle rich, the social class with no need of a job

explanation.definitionFit: Leisured means having ample free time, and the leisured classes are wealthy people without employment.

clue.text: Rows with author over possible obstacles in water

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the author's name above the next piece

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist
banks are rows, as of oars or keys

explanation.surface: A writer quarrels about hazards at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels but means tiers; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandbanks are shoals that can ground boats, hazards to shipping.

clue.text: Open, season, for Americans dropping in by air, naturally

parts.note: free means open, as in free to all
fall is the US word for autumn

explanation.surface: Americans arriving for the open season by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Freefall is descent under gravity alone, as a skydiver before the parachute opens.

clue.text: Performance of clerical duties in 2 government department

definitions.meaning: the work of a minister of religion
an office of state headed by a minister

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a pastor's service to a church and a branch of government such as Defence.

clue.text: Two ways to catch a duck

indicators.note: to catch means the two ways close around the article

parts.note: a mall is a shaded walk or avenue
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Two methods for trapping a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two ways' supplies two separate words for routes; 'to catch' has them close round the A. A mall is also a London avenue, The Mall.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck with a green-headed drake.

clue.text: Men one had initially picked out for baseball team, perhaps

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the three words is plucked away

explanation.surface: Players once selected for a baseball side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially picked out' removes M, O and H from 'Men one had'. A baseball team fields nine, and the definition means a set of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a group of nine, and a baseball side fields nine players.

clue.text: Expression of dismay as girl overturns in river

indicators.note: in puts the turned name inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: overturns says the girl's name is turned upside down, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Myra is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl capsizes in a river, prompting a cry of alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturns' makes ARYM from MYRA, which goes 'in' DEE; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The old-fashioned exclamation voices mild distress or surprise, like 'oh dear'.

clue.text: Issue raised by this member of House cannot succeed

definitions.text: Issue raised by this member of House cannot succeed

parts.words: Issue raised by this member of House cannot succeed
parts.note: reads like a debate point, but issue means children: a peerage held only for life cannot pass to heirs

explanation.walkthrough: House means the House of Lords; a title granted for life only is not inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Lords whose title dies with them leaves nothing for children to inherit.

clue.text: Approach a vendor's position, by the way

definitions.meaning: a sales line or way of persuading

definitions.text: a vendor's position, by the way
definitions.meaning: a street trader's spot at the roadside

explanation.definitionFit: A salesman's spiel and a stallholder's regular patch are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Inability to resolve trouble with university graduate returning

indicators.note: returning says the whole string of pieces runs backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Troubled indecision on coming back from university with a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns AILUBA round; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abulia is a medical term for loss of willpower, being unable to make decisions.

clue.text: Lady, one originally named after kingdom she inhabited

definitions.text: Lady, one originally named after kingdom she inhabited

parts.words: Lady, one originally named after kingdom she inhabited
parts.note: a woman's name that first meant a woman from an ancient kingdom of Asia Minor

explanation.walkthrough: The name first meant a woman from the ancient kingdom in western Asia Minor ruled by Croesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name derives from the old realm of King Croesus, whose women bore it.

clue.text: Miss a game of cards if old

definitions.text: a game of cards if old
definitions.meaning: with old in front it names the children's card game

explanation.definitionFit: A girl or unmarried woman is the archaic sense, and Old Maid is a card game.

clue.text: Signal that may be red

parts.note: a warning that can be of the highest, red, level

explanation.definitionFit: A warning signal, and red is the most urgent grade of such a warning.

clue.text: When everything in the garden gets watered, save for this?

definitions.text: When everything in the garden gets watered, save for this?

parts.words: When everything in the garden gets watered, save for this?
parts.note: a wet day waters the garden, and the idiom says one saves money for hard times

explanation.walkthrough: 'save for' looks like 'except', but it is 'put money aside for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving for hard times is the idiom, and wet weather is what waters plants.

clue.text: Half of forest lies dead, much destroyed as possible result of it.

definitions.text: Half of forest lies dead, much destroyed as possible result of it.

indicators.note: destroyed says the gathered letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
half of picks the second three letters of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: Half a woodland dies from a blight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes EST from 'forest'; 'destroyed' rearranges EST with LIES DEAD MUCH. Read whole, the clue describes the tree blight.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungal blight spread by beetles killed millions of trees, leaving woodland dead.
